To **model** a money problem: say what you need to find, choose the calculation, work it out, then check the answer makes sense in the situation.

- **Pay:** pay = rate × hours. Overtime at "time and a half" pays 1.5 × the rate.
- **Income tax** (simplified from [Australia's 2026–27 resident rates, ATO](https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-australian-residents), which leave out the 2% Medicare levy):

| Income | Rate on that part |
|---|---|
| \$0 to \$18 200 | 0% |
| \$18 201 to \$45 000 | 15% |
| \$45 001 to \$135 000 | 30% |
| \$135 001 to \$190 000 | 37% |
| over \$190 000 | 45% |

The **marginal rate** is the rate on the last dollar; the **effective rate** is all the tax as a percentage of the income.

## Predict: one more dollar

```step
stage: predict
insight: "Committing to what happens when income crosses a bracket shows whether they think the whole income is taxed at the higher rate."
check:
  type: predict
  q: "Your income goes from $45 000 to $45 001, into the 30% bracket. What happens to your tax?"
  options: ["It goes up 30 cents: only the extra dollar is taxed at 30%", "All $45 001 is now taxed at 30%", "You pay less tax", "Nothing changes"]
  actual: "It goes up 30 cents. Only the part above $45 000 is taxed at 30%; the rest is taxed as before."
```

## Run: tax on an income

```step
stage: run
insight: "Moving the income across brackets shows each part taxed at its own rate, and the effective rate staying below the marginal rate."
try: { playground: board, starter: "tax.yml#run", height: 560 }
check: { type: board, text: "Set the income to $60 000. Read the tax and the two rates. Was your prediction right?", when: "i = 60000", explain: "Tax $8520: the marginal rate is 30%, but the effective rate is 8520 ÷ 60 000 = 14.2%." }
```

Each **part** of the income is taxed at its own rate, so only the part above a threshold pays the higher rate.

## Investigate: marginal and effective

```step
stage: investigate
insight: "Tax is added up part by part (Jay taxes the whole income at the top rate); marginal and effective rates answer different questions."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: number
      q: "What is the tax on an income of $30 000, in dollars?"
      answer: 1770
      tolerance: 0
      feedback:
        - ["4500", "The first $18 200 is tax-free: only $11 800 is taxed at 15%."]
      explain: "30 000 − 18 200 = 11 800, and 15% of 11 800 = $1770."
  - check:
      type: bug
      code: "working.txt#jay"
      text: "Jay works out his tax. Click the line where his model goes wrong."
      answer: 3
      fault: logic
      misconception: tax-whole-income
      explain: "Line 3: only the part above $45 000 is taxed at 30%. Tax = 15% of 26 800 + 30% of 5000 = 4020 + 1500 = $5520."
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "Someone earns $60 000. Why is their effective tax rate (14.2%) lower than their marginal rate (30%)?"
      options: ["Most of their income is taxed at 0% or 15%; only the top part is taxed at 30%", "The marginal rate is wrong", "Effective rates are always half the marginal rate", "Because of the Medicare levy"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "It is the rate on the last dollar: 30%.", "There is no such rule.", "The model leaves the levy out."]
      explain: "The lower brackets pull the average down."
```

### Tax on $30 000

Here is the routine.

```worked
60\,000 - 45\,000 = 15\,000 :: The part in the 30% bracket.
26\,800 \times 0.15 = 4020 :: The part from $18 200 to $45 000, at 15%.
15\,000 \times 0.30 = 4500 :: The top part, at 30%.
4020 + 4500 = 8520 :: Add the parts: the tax.
8520 \div 60\,000 = 14.2\% :: The effective rate.
```

### Find the mistake

Read Jay's working. Which part of his income is in the 30% bracket?

## Modify: brackets and pay

```step
stage: modify
insight: "Finding incomes with given taxes and rates, then modelling pay with a rate, hours and overtime."
try: { playground: board, starter: "tax.yml#free", height: 560 }
tasks:
  - starter: "tax.yml#free"
    hint: "Where does the 15% bracket end?"
    check: { type: board, text: "Find the income at the top of the 15% bracket. What is the tax there?", when: "i = 45000", explain: "15% of 26 800 = $4020." }
  - starter: "tax.yml#free"
    hint: ["Try $90 000, then go higher.", "Watch the effective rate as the income passes $90 000."]
    check: { type: board, text: "Find an income whose effective tax rate is more than 20%.", when: "e > 20", explain: "Any income above about $94 800: at $95 000, 19 020 ÷ 95 000 ≈ 20.02%; at $100 000, 20.52%." }
  - starter: "tax.yml#pay"
    check: { type: board, text: "A job pays $28.50 an hour. Set the board for 12 hours. What is the pay?", when: "r = 28.5 and h = 12", explain: "28.50 × 12 = $342." }
  - check:
      type: number
      q: "Overtime is paid at time and a half. How much is 3 hours of overtime at a rate of $28.50, in dollars?"
      answer: 128.25
      tolerance: 0
      explain: "1.5 × 28.50 = $42.75 an hour, × 3 = $128.25."
```

## Practise: money models

```step
stage: practise
insight: "Tax, the effective rate and judging the model, mixed; taxing the whole income at the top rate is the planted slip; the percentage review keeps multipliers fresh."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: number
      q: "What is the tax on $100 000, in dollars?"
      answer: 20520
      tolerance: 0
      feedback:
        - ["30000", "Only the part above $45 000 is taxed at 30%."]
      explain: "4020 + 30% of 55 000 = 4020 + 16 500 = $20 520."
  - check:
      type: number
      q: "What is the effective tax rate on $100 000, as a percentage to 2 decimal places?"
      answer: 20.52
      tolerance: 0.01
      explain: "20 520 ÷ 100 000 = 20.52%."
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "How could this tax model be improved to match a real tax bill?"
      options: ["Add the Medicare levy and tax offsets", "Tax everything at the top rate", "Remove the tax-free part", "Use one rate for everyone"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "That is not how Australian tax works.", "The tax-free part is real.", "Australia uses brackets."]
      explain: "The model leaves out the Medicare levy (usually 2%) and offsets, so real tax is a bit different."
  - check:
      type: number
      q: "Review: decrease $250 by 12%. What is the new amount, in dollars?"
      answer: 220
      tolerance: 0
      explain: "250 × 0.88 = $220."
  - check:
      type: number
      q: "A bank account is overdrawn: its balance is −$120. Then $85 is paid in and a $40 fee is taken. What is the balance now, in dollars?"
      answer: -75
      tolerance: 0
      feedback:
        - ["-5", "The fee is taken away: −120 + 85 − 40."]
      explain: "−120 + 85 − 40 = −75: still overdrawn, by $75."
```

## Make: $50 000 to spend

```step
stage: make
insight: "Searching for an income with a given after-tax amount uses the model in reverse and checks it in context."
try: { playground: board, starter: "tax.yml#free", height: 560 }
hint: ["Income after tax = income − tax.", "Try incomes between $55 000 and $60 000."]
check: { type: board, text: "Find an income (to the nearest $1000) that leaves about $50 000 after tax: between $49 500 and $50 500.", when: "n > 49500 and n < 50500", explain: "$58 000: tax 4020 + 3900 = $7920, leaving $50 080." }
```

Then say whether your answer makes sense, and what the model leaves out.

## Make: a first job's tax, on paper

```step
stage: make
insight: "A first pay slip is tax in brackets. The paper task makes them split the salary into parts and pick which part pays the higher rate."
hint: ["Split \\$52 000 at \\$18 200 and at \\$45 000.", "Only the part above \\$45 000 is taxed at 30%."]
check:
  type: reasoning
  paper: true
  q: "A first full-time job pays \\$52 000 a year. Using the rates in this lesson (no Medicare levy), how many dollars of income tax are taken in a year?"
  steps:
    - ["The first \\$18 200 is taxed at 0%", "the tax-free part"]
    - ["$45 000 - 18 200 = 26 800$, and $26 800 \\times 0.15 = 4020$", "this part is taxed at 15%"]
    - ["$52 000 - 45 000 = 7000$, and $7000 \\times 0.30 = 2100$", "only the part above \\$45 000 is taxed at 30%"]
    - ["$4020 + 2100 = 6120$ dollars of tax, leaving \\$45 880", "add the parts, then take the tax from the salary"]
  picks:
    - step: 3
      q: "How much of the \\$52 000 is taxed at 30%?"
      options:
        - "\\$7000: only the part above \\$45 000"
        - "All \\$52 000, because the salary is in the 30% bracket"
        - "\\$33 800: everything above the tax-free \\$18 200"
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "Each part is taxed at its own rate. The first \\$45 000 is not taxed at 30%.", "The part from \\$18 200 to \\$45 000 is taxed at 15%, not 30%."]
  answer: "6120"
  answerLabel: "Income tax for the year ($)"
  tolerance: 0
  feedback:
    - ["15600", "That taxes the whole \\$52 000 at 30%. Only the part above \\$45 000 is taxed at 30%."]
    - ["2100", "That is the tax on the top part only. Add the tax on the 15% part too."]
    - ["45880", "That is what is left after tax. The question asks for the tax."]
  criteria:
    - "I split the salary into the three parts before multiplying."
    - "I taxed only \\$7000 at 30% and left the first \\$18 200 untaxed."
    - "I added the parts to get the tax, and took it from \\$52 000 for the take-home pay."
  explain: "0 + \\$4020 + \\$2100 = \\$6120. That leaves \\$45 880 a year. A real pay slip also takes the Medicare levy, which this model leaves out, so check the ATO's calculator."
```

Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The salary is made up for the task, but everyone with a first job meets this question when they see how much pay is taken out. Split the salary into parts, tax each one, add them, and type the tax.

**Also used in**

- **Pay slips.** Casual and part-time pay takes tax out in the same brackets, using the rate and the hours worked.
- **Pay rises.** The 'higher bracket' worry is answered by the marginal rate: only the extra dollars are taxed more.
- **Budgets.** What is left after tax is the number a person plans their rent and saving from.

```teacher
summary: Students model pay and income tax in brackets, compare marginal and
  effective rates, and judge what a simple tax model leaves out (AC9M8N05, node
  2).
time: 40
timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 10 min · Practise
  and Make 12 min
goals:
  - I can work out income tax across brackets.
  - I can explain the difference between the marginal and effective rate.
  - I can model pay with a rate, hours and overtime, and check the answer makes
    sense.
struggle: Taxing parts, not the whole. Ask students to split the income into the
  bracket parts on paper before they calculate.
before: >
  Do the Run board yourself first. Students need percentage change (previous
  lesson).


  The one idea: each part of the income is taxed at its own bracket's rate, so
  crossing into a higher bracket never lowers take-home pay. The common mistake
  is taxing the whole income at the top rate (Jay's mistake).


  The board uses a simplified version of Australia's 2026–27 resident rates (0%,
  15%, 30%, 37%, 45%, with thresholds $18 200, $45 000, $135 000, $190 000),
  without the Medicare levy or offsets. Check the ATO's current rates before
  quoting them as exact; the 15% rate is legislated to fall to 14% from 1 July
  2027.


  Wider: effective rates across incomes as a graph; superannuation
  contributions.
running:
  - "Predict: ask what happens to the first $45 000 when income passes it."
  - "Run: ask which rate goes up in steps and which rises smoothly."
  - "Investigate: ask Jay to split his income into parts."
  - "Modify: ask why time and a half is × 1.5."
  - "Make: ask what the model leaves out."
  - "Paper: the first-job tax task is worked in books; the page marks the answer
    ($6120) and which part of the salary pays 30%. Books out, then look for the
    salary split into three parts."
stuck:
  - see: A student taxes the whole income at the top rate.
    ask: Which part of the income is in the top bracket?
    fix: Split the income into bracket parts; tax each part.
  - see: A student forgets the tax-free part.
    ask: How much is taxed at 0%?
    fix: Start from $18 200.
  - see: A student mixes up marginal and effective.
    ask: Is that the rate on the last dollar, or the share of all the income?
    fix: "Marginal: last dollar. Effective: tax ÷ income."
stretch: Plot the effective rate for incomes from $20 000 to $200 000. Why does
  it rise smoothly when the marginal rate jumps?
support: "A table with one row per bracket: the part of the income, the rate, the tax."
leads: >
  This completes AC9M8N05.


  Where it leads: financial mathematics in Years 9 and 10 (interest, budgets),
  and modelling with rates.
exit:
  q: Tax is 0% on the first $18 200 of income, 15% on the next part up to $45 000,
    and 30% on the part from $45 000 to $135 000. Find the tax on $50 000.
  a: "15% of (45 000 − 18 200) = 15% of 26 800 = $4020, plus 30% of 5000 = $1500:
    $5520 in all."
explain: >
  To **model** a money problem: decide what to find, choose the calculation,
  work it out, and check it makes sense.


  Income tax is worked out in **brackets**: each part of the income is taxed at
  its own rate. The **marginal rate** is the rate on the last dollar; the
  **effective rate** is total tax ÷ income, which is lower (for incomes above
  $18 200).
sources:
  - title: Tax rates – Australian residents (ATO)
    url: https://www.ato.gov.au/tax-rates-and-codes/tax-rates-australian-residents
    checked: 2026-10-12
  - title: Income tax rates and brackets, including the 14% rate from 1 July 2027
      (SuperGuide)
    url: https://www.superguide.com.au/how-super-works/income-tax-rates-brackets
    checked: 2026-10-12
```
